- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; adjust downward bias by 5–10% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.24), model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1–3 day lagged mean reversion term to forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, model tends to lag; shift forecast horizon down by 1–3 days if sentiment is weak.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >15% from model in first 5 days, apply “early correction” rule: reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for next 3 days.
